_readme: Draft wake-phrase list for Kora. Nothing here is trained yet: each enabled phrase must be trained as its own custom keyword in the Picovoice Console (Porcupine), which produces one .ppn file per phrase and platform.
Save each trained file under frontend/assets/wake/ using the file name in the 'ppn' field, one per platform (for example hey_kora_android.ppn and hey_kora_ios.ppn).

To add your own phrase, copy any entry, change 'phrase', 'id' and 'ppn', and set 'enabled' to true. The app should load only entries that are enabled AND whose file exists, so an entry without a trained file is safely skipped.
Porcupine matches only the exact trained phrase. It cannot detect arbitrary greeting words, so every greeting a rider might use needs its own entry.

Guidance: phrases of 3 to 4 syllables or more give the fewest false triggers and misses. A bare 'Kora' is only 2 syllables and may fire on similar sounds or on road and cab noise, so train it, but start with a sensitivity around 0.5 and raise it only if it misses. Check your Picovoice plan for how many custom keywords you may train and run at once, and start with the tier 1 entries.
Say the phrase the way your riders say it. If riders pronounce it differently (KOH-ra versus KOR-ah), train both spellings as separate entries, or set the pronunciation in the Console.

phrases.note: Recommended primary. Natural, clear syllable count, the pattern people already know from other assistants.
